clue.text: Unrested, somehow, set to come out at night

definitions.text: set to come out at night

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the first word are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: An insomniac, still unrested, is somehow expected to go out on the town after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'set' as a set of teeth, the kind many people take out before bed.
explanation.definitionFit: False teeth form a set that wearers often remove and soak overnight.

clue.text: Title state expunged from essay and paper

indicators.note: expunged from says the word for state is struck out of the next word

parts.note: to state is to say
a quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: A title about the state was struck out of an essay and a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesy honorific placed after a gentleman's name, as in letters.

clue.text: Dangerous influence monarch introduced to all French

indicators.note: introduced to says the other pieces are put inside the French word

parts.note: tous is French for all
reach is influence, scope
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch's perilous influence is brought to bear on all the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacherous ground or ice is hazardous, unsafe to cross.

clue.text: Considers vermin circling base of tree

indicators.note: circling says the vermin word surrounds the letter

parts.note: rats are vermin

indicators.note: base of, in a down clue, picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone eyes the rats gathering round the foot of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to judge or regard it a certain way.

clue.text: Small bed and leash for dog

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a tie is something that tethers, like a leash

explanation.surface: A shopper buys a little bed and a lead for the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish terrier is a breed of small dog.

clue.text: One managing to contain phosphorus in large vessel

indicators.note: to contain says the first piece wraps around the chemical symbol

parts.note: a coper is one who copes, i.e. manages
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A works manager arranges to store phosphorus in a big tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A copper was a large metal boiler, traditionally used for washing laundry.

clue.text: Old soldier, one with punishing schedule, maybe, nobody welcomed

indicators.note: welcomed says the word for nobody is taken in by the other piece

parts.note: a caner is one who canes, as a strict teacher might routinely do
none means nobody

explanation.surface: A veteran, perhaps a strict disciplinarian, was welcomed by nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the caner as just one example of a person who punishes routinely.
explanation.definitionFit: An artilleryman who fired big guns was a soldier of former times.

clue.text: Postie occasionally delivers foreign letter

indicators.note: occasionally says only every other letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: The postman sometimes brings a letter from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: A postie is British slang for a postman.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenty-third character of the Greek alphabet, so a letter that is not English.

clue.text: Endless ale drunk before and after reported act

indicators.note: before and after says the scrambled drink is split, part ahead of and part behind the other piece
drunk says the drink's letters are reeling into a new order
reported says the word for act is heard, giving a seabird spelling

parts.note: a turn is an act on stage

explanation.surface: Endless ale is drunk before and after a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' scrambles ale into EAL, split E and AL around the seabird; 'reported' makes the stage act sound like that bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without end lasts for ever, so it is everlasting.

clue.text: Search on northern river keeps one in form

indicators.note: keeps says the string built from the other pieces holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: a quest is a search
taken as written
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A search along a river in the north keeps someone in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In form' sounds like fitness, but 'form' alone is the definition: a document to fill in.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey sheet of questions is a kind of form people fill in.

clue.text: Fish food with crust son Charlie tucks into

indicators.note: tucks into says the two letters go inside the food word, with a hint of eating

parts.note: pies are food with a pastry crust
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A boy named Charlie tucks into fish pie with a crust.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign of the Fishes is the plural Latin word for fish.

clue.text: Traveller cutting steak produces an instrument

indicators.note: cutting says the traveller's word slices into the steak

parts.note: a T-bone is a cut of steak
a Rom is a Romani traveller

explanation.surface: A traveller carving a steak somehow ends up producing a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The slide brass horn is a musical instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: Sign of illegitimacy as wickedness is evident in deal

indicators.note: evident in says the following pieces appear inside the word for deal

parts.note: to barter is to trade or deal
sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: A shady trade shows wickedness, a sign of something illegitimate.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a diagonal band on a coat of arms was said to mark a bastard line.

clue.text: African seen buffeted by winds close to village

indicators.note: buffeted says the letters are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: gales are strong winds

indicators.note: close to picks the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An African traveller is seen battered by gales near a village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffeted' rearranges only SEEN, into SENE; 'winds' is not the anagram signal but gives GALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Senegal in West Africa is an African.

clue.text: Anti-Royalist battle?

parts.note: agin is dialect for against, anti
the court is the royal household and its party, the king's side

explanation.surface: A battle fought by opponents of the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the battle's name as 'agin court', against the royal court. The question mark flags this playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V's 1415 victory over the French was a famous battle.

clue.text: Smaller runner runs poorly

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A slower athlete runs badly in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is water that runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny brook is a lesser flowing stream than a river.

clue.text: Grain used in pudding: try it first

indicators.note: first says the word for it comes before the word for try

parts.note: it means sex appeal, SA
a go is a try

explanation.surface: A cook recommends tasting a pudding grain before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy granules from palm pith are cooked in milk as a traditional pudding.

clue.text: Christian missionary throwing stone into a bar

indicators.note: throwing says the weight is tossed in among the other letters
into says where the stone lands, inside the other pieces

parts.note: a pole is a bar
ST is the abbreviation for stone, a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A missionary hurls a stone into a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the first followers sent to spread the Gospel.

clue.text: Dictatorial nurses see proof

indicators.note: nurses means holds close, so the first word cradles the abbreviation

parts.note: imperious means dictatorial, domineering
V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: Bossy nurses demand to see evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proof' looks like a noun meaning evidence; it is the adjective, as in waterproof.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof as an adjective means resistant, letting nothing through.

clue.text: Organic fuel around lake man gathered

indicators.note: around says the fuel word goes about the letter

parts.note: peat is a fuel formed from decayed plants
Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man collected peat for fuel around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathered' looks like collecting; it is the dressmaking sense of folded fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt with folds pressed in is gathered into pleats.

clue.text: Open about amount of work experience

indicators.note: about says the word for open goes round the unit

parts.note: to undo is to open
an erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Being candid about how much work there is shows experience.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to go through or suffer it.

clue.text: Remains here when rogue returns, having caught on

indicators.note: returns says the words for when and rogue are read backwards together

parts.note: as means when
a dog is a rogue or scoundrel
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A villain who comes back gets caught and stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' is not a verb but a noun: the bodies of the dead lie here.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for a churchyard, where buried remains lie.

clue.text: Sandy, also going to hold back in quarrel

indicators.note: to hold says the shortened name wraps around the word for back
going says the word for also leaves the name

parts.note: and means also
hind means back, rear

explanation.surface: Sandy is also drawn into a row but holds back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going' removes AND from SANDY to leave SY, which then holds HIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated informal word for a noisy row or brawl.

clue.text: Sporty sort to steal tuppence from captain?

indicators.note: to steal says the coins are taken away from the other piece
from says which word the coins are lifted out of

parts.note: a skipper is a captain
two pence, P being the abbreviation for penny, so PP

explanation.surface: An athletic type is accused of pinching small change from the team captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the slopes is a winter sportsperson.

clue.text: Stuttering woe corrected in diction exercise

indicators.note: corrected says the letters are put right by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A speech therapist corrects a stammerer's troubles with practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-to-say phrase is used to practise clear pronunciation.

clue.text: Fortune trader keeps after taxes

indicators.note: keeps says the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A trader keeps his fortune once taxes are paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Net pay is what remains once deductions have been taken.

clue.text: Get morsel to chew as filling

indicators.note: as filling says the chewing word is the stuffing inside the morsel

parts.note: a bit is a morsel
to eat is to chew

explanation.surface: Someone is told to grab a bite to munch as a sandwich filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' reads as a verb of fetching; it is the order 'Get!', go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are curt commands telling someone to clear off.

clue.text: Night fell over development area

parts.note: night is the dark

indicators.note: over says the upland word is turned back to front

parts.note: a fell is an upland moor

explanation.surface: Darkness fell over an area earmarked for building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past of fall, but it is a hill moor. 'Development' is photographic, not property.
explanation.definitionFit: Film is developed in a lightless room set aside for processing photographs.
